episodes.title: The King Who Made Himself a Bridge
sources: Mahakapi Jataka (No. 407), in The Jataka, ed. E. B. Cowell, Vol. III, tr. H. T. Francis and R. A. Neil (Cambridge University Press, 1897), pp. 225-227; read 2026-11-16 at https://ancient-buddhist-texts.net/English-Texts/Jataka/407.htm
A. Cunningham, The Stupa of Bharhut (1879), plate XXXIII, fig. 4 (as cited in the translators' headnote to Jataka 407)

quiz.q: How did the troop cross the river?
quiz.why: The bamboo fell short, so he held a branch and made his own body the last span.

quiz.q: Which idea does the story stand for in an ethics answer?
options: Power is a duty to those you lead
A leader must never take risks
Loyalty is owed only to the ruler
quiz.why: The monkey king says the troop's happiness was his task; the king learns the same of his people.

quiz.q: Where is this scene carved in stone?
quiz.why: The video names the stupa at Bharhut, carved over two thousand years ago.

episodes.title: Rani ki Vav: Six Ideas in Stone
sources: UNESCO World Heritage List, entry 922, "Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen's Stepwell) at Patan, Gujarat", https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/922/ (read 2026-11-16)
World Heritage Committee, Decision 38 COM 8B.25 (Doha, 2014), https://whc.unesco.org/en/decisions/6111 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Why is Rani ki Vav called an inverted temple?
options: Its tower was built upside down
You go down towards water held sacred
It faces west instead of east
It was rebuilt after a flood
quiz.why: UNESCO describes it as designed as an inverted temple highlighting the sanctity of water.

quiz.q: What preserved its carving for centuries?
quiz.why: The Saraswati shifted and flood silt filled the stepwell, which kept the sculpture safe.

quiz.q: In which year was it put on UNESCO's World Heritage List?
quiz.why: It was inscribed in 2014, at the Committee's session in Doha.

episodes.title: The Monsoon's Journey
sources: India Meteorological Department, press release "New normal dates of onset/progress and withdrawal of southwest monsoon over India" (April 2020), station table, https://mausam.imd.gov.in/backend/assets/press_release_pdf/IMD_Press_release_new_onset_and_withdrawal_dates%28Final%29.pdf (read 2026-11-16)
NCERT, Class XI, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 "Climate"

quiz.q: Where does the monsoon normally arrive first on the mainland?
quiz.why: The normal onset over Kerala is 1 June; the video starts at Thiruvananthapuram.

quiz.q: Why does the Bay of Bengal branch move west up the Ganga plain?
quiz.why: Turned by the Arakan hills and then the Himalaya, it travels west along the Ganga plain.

quiz.q: By IMD's 2020 calendar, when does the monsoon normally cover the far north-west?
quiz.why: The new normal date is 8 July; the older calendar said 15 July.

episodes.title: I Am a Harappan Seal
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part I (Class XII), Theme 1 'Bricks, Beads and Bones', reprint 2020-21, sections 6, 7.1, 7.2, 10.1, 10.2 (archive.org/details/ncert-lehs1, read 2026-11-16)
John Marshall (ed.), Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization, Vol. I (1931), pp. 31-32 and 67-68 (archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.722, read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: How was a seal used to protect goods in trade?
options: It was hung around the trader's neck
It was pressed into wet clay on the knot of a tied sack
It was painted on the side of the boat
It was given to the buyer as payment
quiz.why: An unbroken sealing on the knot showed nobody had opened the sack, and who had sent it.

quiz.q: Why is the Harappan script thought not to be an alphabet?
options: It is written in Greek letters
It has too many signs, nearly 400
It was never written on seals
quiz.why: NCERT notes 375 to 400 signs: too many for letters standing for single sounds.

quiz.q: What stone were most Harappan seals cut from?
quiz.why: Seals were made of steatite, a soft stone, finished with a hard white coating.

episodes.title: The Bronze Dancer of Mohenjo-daro
sources: NCERT, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I (Class XI), ch. 2 'Arts of the Indus Valley', sections 'Bronze casting' and the 'Dancing Girl' caption (archive.org/details/ncert-kefa1, read 2026-11-16)
John Marshall (ed.), Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization, Vol. I (1931), pp. 33-34, 44-45 and plate notes to Pl. XCIV, 6-8 (archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.722, read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Which method was used to cast Harappan bronzes like the Dancing Girl?
quiz.why: A wax figure was coated in clay, the wax melted out, and molten metal poured into the hollow.

quiz.q: About how tall is the Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro?
quiz.why: NCERT calls her approximately four inches high; Marshall's plate note gives 4.25 inches.

quiz.q: Which of these was also cast in bronze by Indus craftspeople, as NCERT notes?
options: A buffalo with its head raised
quiz.why: NCERT names a buffalo with uplifted head and a goat among Indus bronzes.
